previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG and stents, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, diabetes, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for acute chest pain associated with dizziness, nausea, vomiting, and diaphoresis. The pain did not respond to nitroglycerin but resolved with morphine. Initial evaluation showed hypotension, EKG changes including T-wave inversions, and a new left lower lobe opacity on chest X-ray concerning for pneumonia, though the patient remained afebrile without cough or leukocytosis. Cardiac biomarkers showed minimal troponin elevation without significant rise, ruling out acute myocardial infarction. A central line was placed for access after peripheral IV failure. The patient developed left hand pain with coolness and weak pulses, likely related to vascular insufficiency from his dialysis fistula; vascular surgery follow-up was recommended. He remained stable, completed a dialysis session, and was discharged home with instructions to monitor weight, continue medications, and follow up with cardiology and vascular surgery.

Brief Hospital Course:
# Bacteremia: The patient was found to have enterococcal 
bacteremia on multiple positive blood cultures (daily from 
___.  The presumed source was the HD tunneled catheter, 
which had MRSA and enterococcus on tip Cx.  Infectious disease 
was consulted and pt was started on HD dosed vancomycin with 
gentamycin for synergy.  Surveillance blood cultures cleared on 
this regimen. TEE demonstrated a vegetation on his pacer which 
was explanted on ___.  Pt will continued Abx therapy for 6 
weeks from this date and will be dosed with Vancomycin 1gram IV 
qHD and Gentamicin 40 mg IV qHD, last dose ___.  Patient 
has follow-up scheduled with ID for weekly follow-up labs, 
including CBC with diff, LFTs, ESR, CRP, vancomycin trough and 
gentamicin trough will be drawn at HD and faxed to ___ clinic.

# Pacemaker removal: Given vegetations on pacemaker leads and 
ongoing bacteremia, device was removed without incident. Patient 
monitored for 48 hours on telemetry without incident following 
the removal.  He is to follow-up with Dr. ___ in 2 weeks 
for wound check and suture removal. (appointment to be arranged 
post-discharge)

# Peripheral Neuropathy: Pregabalin was increased to 25mg BID 
with better symptom control.

# Chest Pain: The patient had multiple episodes of chest pain 
that were clinically thought to be consistent with esophageal 
spasm. He was ruled out for an MI on two separate occasions and 
never had EKG changes during this stay.  Pt was ambulating chest 
pain free by the time of discharge.

#  Back Pain: Images negative for any infectious etiology.  
Clinical examination suggestive of intermittent muscle spasm.  
Pain improved with low-dose ativan and pt will be following up 
with PCP this week.

# ESRD: Continued on HD T/H/S throughout hospitalization and 
followed by the renal team.  Pt will be having labs drawn weekly 
during his HD sessions - including CBC with diff, LFTs, ESR, 
CRP, vancomycin trough and gentamicin trough which will be faxed 
to ID at ___.  He will be recieving Vancomycin 1g IV 
qHD and gentamicin 40 mg IV qHD for treatment of his 
endocarditis.  Treatment course will be 6 weeks, last dose 
___.

# PVD:  Foot ulcers treated with silvadene, seen by podiatry, 
not concerned for active foot ulcer infection.  Discharged with 
wound foot care and home ___ evaluation

# L arm steal syndrome:  Pt has ongoing pain in left arm due to 
AV fistula and steal pof blood flow, which has been a chronic 
issue.  He was scheduled to go to OR for ligation.  However, 
this was deferred due to bacteremia and infection of tunneled 
line.  Fistula was accessed for dialysis without problems and pt 
be getting ongoing HD via fistula while receiving antibiotics 
for the endocarditis as above.
.
# CAD s/p CABG: Maintained on home meds

# HTN: Maintained on home regimen.

# IDDM: Continued on insulin sliding scale.

radiology_notes.text:
LUMBAR SPINE.

INDICATION:  Right low back pain.

FINDINGS:  Radiographs in the frontal and lateral projection are obtained. 
Single stent in the right common iliac artery.  Multiple stents in the left
common iliac artery.  Massive vascular calcifications in the entire abdomen.

Mild spondylophyte formation at the anterior aspect of the vertebral bodies. 
No evidence of vertebral collapse.  Moderate-to-severe degenerative changes of
the intervertebral joints.

INDICATION:  ___ male with bacteremia and right sacroiliac joint
tenderness.  The patient is unable to receive an MRI as he has an ICD.  CT is
requested to evaluate for evidence of right SI or right hip joint infection.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Post-contrast imaging of the pelvis was performed with the
administration of 100 mL of Optiray contrast.  Multiplanar reformats are
prepared and reviewed.

SOFT TISSUES:

There are bilateral common iliac stents, which are patent.  The left stent
extends into the external iliac.  Additional stents are identified in the
common femoral arteries, also patent.  The intrapelvic loops of large and
small bowel are unremarkable.  There is normal amount of fecal material
identified within the colon.  The appendix is seen in the right lower quadrant
and is normal.  There is no free pelvic fluid and no pelvic fluid collection
identified to suggest abscess.  Distal ureters and bladder, prostate, and
seminal vesicles are unremarkable.  There is no pelvic or inguinal adenopathy.

BONE WINDOWS:

The bones are normally mineralized.  There is no appreciable effusion in the
right or left hip joints.  The sacroiliac joints are similarly unremarkable,
without fluid within or adjacent and without periosteal reaction or cortical
erosion.  There is mild degenerative change seen in the visualized lumbar
spine.

There is soft tissue stranding in the anterior abdominal wall, presumably
reflecting subcutaneous injections.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No evidence for infection involving the bilateral hips or sacroiliac
joints by CT imaging. 

2.  No intrapelvic pathology to explain bacteremia.  No evidence of abscess or
colitis.

3.  Extensive atherosclerosis, with bilateral iliac and femoral arterial
stents.

NOTE: The following preliminary report was issued by Dr. ___ discussed
with Dr. ___ at 9:00 p.m. on ___:  "No CT evidence of
osteomyelitis of right SI or right hip.  No periosteal reaction, erosions,
soft tissue gas, or stranding.  No definite hip effusions.  Right SI joint is
minimally wider than left, however, no irregularity."
